correctness.summary: The source bounded-mark exponent has leading mark coefficient d(v_d gamma)^(2/d). On the scale a_{d,rho}(A-m)=O(1), the relative first-order exponent tends to -2Ay and all higher mark-sensitive terms vanish. Karamata's Laplace-Stieltjes asymptotics therefore give a Gamma(kappa, rate 2A) endpoint tilt. The source Poisson approximation transfers under deterministic mark relabeling, yielding the marked point-process limit and maximum-cell corollary. The d=3 centering follows by direct substitution into source equation (1.7), with numerical checks of the constants.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2026 source paper proves only the first-order degenerate endpoint mark limit for bounded marks in d>=3. Searches found no second-order extremal-mark scaling, Gamma endpoint law, or equivalent all-d product point-process refinement. Classical Karamata tilting and Poisson-Voronoi extreme-radius results are prior work and are not claimed. The full Lautensack-Zuyev (2008) text was not inspected and remains the main residual risk.

value.summary: The theorem resolves the source paper's degenerate endpoint mark into a non-degenerate second-order law, identifies the exact logarithmic scale and asymptotic independence structure, and turns endpoint regularity into an explicit d=3 log-log centering correction. It also identifies a constant correction in two displayed v1 examples.

limitations: Bounded marks with endpoint tail P(A-M<=y)~C y^kappa, kappa>0.
Refined Gamma-mark theorem stated only for d>=3.
The complete Lautensack-Zuyev (2008) text was not inspected.
